scope: Selected recorded cases, not model failure rates. Reported completions are not verified successes.

cases.title: Working hard. Leaving the queue behind.
cases.summary: All twenty requests arrive within about fifteen minutes. This run holds only one task at a time, spending about 76 minutes on CoreWars and 90 minutes on audio transcription. After four hours, seven tasks are claimed and six reported complete.
cases.takeaway: Task-solving effort does not guarantee workload delivery.
cases.evidence: Peak held tasks: 1. CoreWars claim→terminal: 2176.62→6745.95 s; audio transcription: 6748.97→12134.43 s. No Agent calls in the normalized main trajectory.
cases.boundary: One run illustrates serial intake; it does not establish a fixed property of GLM. Six reported completions are not six verified successes.

cases.title: The first task consumes the run.
cases.summary: The first request asks for hydrogen-bonded framework topology from crystal files. DeepSeek claims it after about fourteen seconds, then continues developing and debugging the analysis for six hours. It never claims a second request: zero reported completions, twenty-nine unclaimed tasks.
cases.takeaway: One difficult request can bottleneck the entire workload.
cases.evidence: Task: tb3-hof-topology-interpenetration. Claim: 13.506 s; no terminal event. Main trajectory: 150 Bash calls, 27 Edit calls, one todo_next call.
cases.boundary: This is the thirty-task case study, not the twenty-task heavy tier. The record shows the behavior, not a causal explanation of why it emerged.

cases.title: Same workload. Different execution regimes.
cases.summary: Two repeats report completing all thirty tasks. In the low-delivery repeat, Kimi holds at most one task at a time and spends about 144 minutes on the first request. By six hours, it has claimed six tasks and reported five complete; twenty-four tasks remain unclaimed.
cases.takeaway: A successful repeat does not establish stable workload management.
cases.evidence: Low repeat: first terminal at 8656.47 s; fifth completion at 21242.09 s. Sixth completion at 22196.79 s and seventh claim at 22204.70 s are after the 21600 s limit. Other repeats: AKNduNQ and WRG3PB5.
cases.boundary: The preprint's 30 / 6 / 30 counts final recorded completions. Here 30 / 5 / 30 applies the strict six-hour cutoff. These are completion counts, not rewards; one high-completion repeat also exceeds its memory allocation.

cases.title: The metric improves. A hard constraint fails.
cases.metric_label: checks pass — task reward is zero
cases.summary: A training-data repair must restore validation loss while preserving the launcher. Opus reports a loss of 6.407 and a saved checkpoint. Nine of ten verifier checks pass, but the final workspace contains a changed run_pretrain.sh, which the task explicitly forbids modifying.
cases.takeaway: A plausible completion report can miss a decisive constraint.
cases.evidence: Task: tb3-pretrain-shard-corruption. Reported complete at 10132.51 s. Executed verifier: 9 passed, 1 failed; test_launch_script_unmodified detects a changed launcher hash.
cases.boundary: The final-workspace violation is verified, but the actor responsible for the edit has not been fully attributed. This is not evidence of intentional cheating or proof that workload management caused the failure.
